quickAnswer: Cleaning a 5,000 sq ft US commercial office costs $435 to $870 per visit—or $2,234 to $15,913 per month—across standard weekly to 5x/week weekday schedules (assuming commercial carpet, two restrooms, and the 1.00x national average). Using the 2,500–9,999 sq ft bracket ($0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft) plus $15 to $30 per restroom, a 3x/week suite totals $458 to $772 per visit ($5,948 to $10,042/month over 13.0 visits) and requires 1.55 to 2.29 ISSA crew labor hours.

blocks.text: At **5,000 square feet**, a commercial suite crosses an important operational threshold. Unlike 1,000 to 2,000 sq ft offices where minimum trip charges (`$90 to $135` per visit) distort unit economics, a 5,000 sq ft floorplate clears every contractor's dispatch floor and lands squarely inside the **2,500–9,999 sq ft pricing bracket** at **$0.09 to $0.15 per sq ft**.

For a typical 25- to 40-person office—featuring a reception area, one or two conference rooms, open workstations, a breakroom, and two restrooms—procurement teams can verify any vendor bid against four repeatable inputs: **square-footage bracket**, **restroom surcharge ($15–$30 each)**, **flooring multiplier**, and **frequency multiplier**. If you manage a slightly larger multi-zone suite, compare these figures with our [6,000 sq ft office cost guide](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-6000-sq-ft-office/) or step back to the [national office cleaning cost benchmarks](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/).
5,000 Sq Ft Office Cleaning Cost Breakdown by Schedule

Increasing weekly visits lowers your **per-visit price** while raising total monthly spend. Infrequent accounts—such as monthly (`1.28x`) or biweekly (`1.16x`)—accumulate overflowing desk trash, dried coffee rings, and restroom scale that slow technicians down. By contrast, a 3x/week (`0.95x`) or 5x/week (`0.90x`) schedule lets crews work faster with predictable surface passes.

Notice how monthly retainers multiply per-visit pricing by **4.333 weeks per month** (rounding to `4.33` in calendar tables): `4.33` visits for weekly, `8.66` for twice weekly, `13.00` for 3x/week, and `21.65` for 5x/week weekday service. Any proposal multiplying 3x/week by 12 visits instead of 13.0 either skips fifth weeks or bills extra later.

blocks.title: Why 5,000 Sq Ft Clears Minimum Trip Fees
blocks.text: Even at 5x/week (0.90x), base square-footage labor for 5,000 sq ft runs $405 to $675 before adding $30 to $60 for two restrooms. Because total per-visit billing sits well above the $90 to $135 US minimum trip charge, facility managers gain genuine per-square-foot pricing efficiency rather than paying flat dispatch minimums.
ISSA Crew Labor Hours: Solo Custodian vs. 2-Person Evening Team

Under **ISSA commercial cleaning production standards**, an equipped technician covers roughly **3,500 sq ft per labor hour** in open workstations (`2,800 to 4,000 sq ft/hr` depending on cubicle density), equating to **1.43 floor hours** at 3,500 sq ft/hr. Adding `0.15 to 0.25 hours` per restroom puts credible total labor for a 5,000 sq ft suite with two restrooms at **1.55 to 2.29 labor hours per visit**.

In practice, contractors staff 5,000 sq ft accounts either with one custodian working a **1.75- to 2.25-hour shift** or a two-person evening crew finishing in **45 to 70 clock minutes** (with one technician vacuuming and pulling trash while the second sanitizes restrooms, breakroom counters, and interior glass). When comparing pure **hourly janitorial contracts ($35–$65/hr standard; $55–$95/hr specialty)** against bracket-based quotes, remember that per-square-foot contracts bake supervision, Workers' Compensation, chemical dilution, and equipment depreciation into the unit rate—whereas hourly quotes fluctuate whenever detail tasks slow production below 3,000 sq ft/hr.
How Flooring Surfaces and Scope Add-Ons Shift Your Quote

Floor material is the fastest way two identical 5,000 sq ft suites diverge in monthly spend. **Polished concrete (`0.95x`)** cleans quickly with a wide dust mop and damp pass, whereas **ceramic tile and grout (`1.12x`)** demands manual grout-line agitation that adds **$666 to $1,112 per month** on a 3x/week contract compared with standard carpet tiles.

blocks.text: *All four add-ons at 5,000 sq ft add: **breakroom and kitchenette sanitation** (`+$12–$25/visit`), **interior glass and conference partitions** (`+$15–$35/visit`), **paper and soap consumables** (`+$60–$125/visit` at `$0.012–$0.025/sq ft`), and **amortized quarterly deep floor care** (`+$150–$300/month` at `$0.03–$0.06/sq ft/mo`).
City Market Multipliers and Multi-Suite Comparisons

Because labor consumes two-thirds or more of a cleaning contractor's operating budget, regional wage floors move a 5,000 sq ft quote substantially. Using our national metro index, a 3x/week carpeted suite with two restrooms ranges from **$389 to $657 per visit ($5,055–$8,536/month)** in **0.85x lower-cost Southern markets** up to **$558 to $942 per visit ($7,256–$12,252/month)** in **1.22x hubs** and **$618 to $1,043 per visit ($8,029–$13,557/month)** in **1.35x Tier-1 coastal towers**.

Janitorial Closet Equipment Needed for a 5,000 Sq Ft Suite

Even when your cleaning vendor brings labor, specifying commercial-grade floor tools—or stocking an on-site janitorial closet—protects carpet seams and engineered wood finishes while keeping crew hours within budget. Pair fast dry debris pickup (see our [Rubbermaid 421288 vs. Bissell BG23 sweeper comparison](/commercial-vacuums-and-floor-machines/rubbermaid-421288-vs-bissell-bg23-sweeper/)) with color-coded wet-mopping gear so restroom bacteria never migrate into breakrooms or executive boardrooms:

items: **Rubbermaid Commercial WaveBrake 35-Quart Mop Bucket & Side-Press Wringer:** Built with a 35-quart splash-reducing baffled tub, side-press wringer profile, and 5-year wringer duty rating tested for 200,000+ cycles—ideal for hard-floor restrooms and kitchenettes.

**Rubbermaid Commercial HYGEN Charging Bucket:** Holds up to 20 color-coded microfiber flat-mop pads under a tight snap lid for OSHA-ready pre-soak chemical dosing without dipping dirty mops back into clean solution.

**O-Cedar ProMist MAX Commercial Microfiber Spray Mop:** Uses a 14.5-inch double-sided, machine-washable microfiber pad with an onboard refillable bottle for low-moisture spot cleaning on engineered hardwood conference rooms.

blocks.title: Verify COI, HazCom SDS, and Restroom Biohazard Rules
blocks.text: Before handing over suite keys, require an active Certificate of Insurance ($1M/$2M General Liability naming your company and landlord as Additional Insured, plus Workers' Compensation and a fidelity bond), OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200) Safety Data Sheets for every diluted chemical in your closet, and OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) protocols for restroom spill response.
5 Steps to Audit Any 5,000 Sq Ft Cleaning Quote

items.name: Confirm Net Cleanable Square Footage
items.text: Separate net suite area from landlord-maintained elevator lobbies, stairwells, and shared restrooms so you only pay for spaces your vendor actually services.

items.name: Match Visit Math to 4.333 Weeks per Month
items.text: Divide monthly retainers by 13.0 (for 3x/week) or 21.65 (for 5x/week) to verify true per-visit rates and confirm fifth-week coverage is included.

items.name: Check Implied Crew Hours Against 1.55–2.29 Hours
items.text: Ask bidders for exact evening staffing hours per visit; ultra-cheap bids below $250/visit usually rely on 45-minute rush sweeps or unbonded 1099 labor.

items.name: Lock Restroom, Glass, and Breakroom Specifications
items.text: Spell out fixture counts, microwave/fridge wipe-downs, and conference glass height in the Statement of Work to block surprise add-on invoices.

items.name: Benchmark Consumables Separately From Labor
items.text: Compare vendor-supplied tissue, towels, soap, and liners ($60–$125/visit at 5,000 sq ft) against direct wholesale ordering before bundling supplies.

faqs.q: How much does it cost per month to clean a 5,000 sq ft office?
faqs.a: At the 1.00x US national average for commercial carpet with two restrooms, a 5,000 sq ft office costs $2,234 to $3,767 per month for 1x/week service, $4,157 to $7,015 for 2x/week, $5,948 to $10,042 for 3x/week (13.0 visits/month), and $9,418 to $15,913 for 5x/week weekday service (21.65 visits/month), before optional consumables or quarterly deep floor care.

faqs.q: How long should a crew take to clean a 5,000 sq ft office?
faqs.a: Based on ISSA production standards (2,800 to 4,000 sq ft per labor hour plus 0.15 to 0.25 hours per restroom), a 5,000 sq ft suite with two restrooms requires 1.55 to 2.29 total labor hours per visit. One technician finishes in roughly 1.75 to 2.25 hours, while a two-person team completes the scope in about 50 to 70 minutes.

faqs.q: Why do vendors use 4.333 weeks per month instead of 4 weeks when quoting 5,000 sq ft suites?
faqs.a: Because a 52-week year averages 4.333 weeks per month (4.33 in rounded estimators). Multiplying 3 visits/week by 4.333 yields 13.0 visits/month, and 5 visits/week yields 21.65 visits/month—ensuring flat monthly invoicing covers four-week and five-week calendar months evenly.

faqs.q: What insurance and OSHA compliance documents must a janitorial contractor provide?
faqs.a: Require a current Certificate of Insurance (COI) with $1,000,000 per occurrence / $2,000,000 aggregate Commercial General Liability naming your company as Additional Insured, statutory Workers' Compensation for W-2 employees, a janitorial fidelity bond, OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200) Safety Data Sheets, and Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) training for restroom sanitation.

faqs.q: What is typically excluded from a standard 5,000 sq ft office cleaning contract?
faqs.a: Routine recurring rates exclude hot-water carpet extraction, VCT floor stripping and waxing (which average $0.03 to $0.06/sq ft/month when amortized quarterly, or $150 to $300/month), interior/exterior high glass above 8 feet, paper and soap consumables ($60 to $125/visit), inside-refrigerator cleanouts, and biohazard remediation unless explicitly listed as add-ons.
